claim_text: In the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, the FDA approval summary reports investigator-assessed median PFS of 11.0 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant versus 5.7 months with placebo plus fulvestrant, but this should be read as an endocrine-resistant, biomarker-selected setting rather than a clean acquired PI3Kalpha-resistance experiment `pmid-33168657`.
evidence_summary: The FDA approval summary of SOLAR-1 reports regular approval after progression on or after endocrine-based therapy and investigator-assessed PFS of 11.0 versus 5.7 months in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort. Limitation: regulatory randomized trial summary, not a mechanistic acquired PI3Kalpha-resistance experiment.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the FDA approval summary.

claim_text: A clinical review of SOLAR-1 similarly emphasizes that patients had prior aromatase inhibitor exposure and endocrine-resistant disease, with improved response and clinical benefit in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort `pmid-32782489`.
evidence_summary: The clinical review describes SOLAR-1 patients as endocrine-resistant after relapse during endocrine therapy or within 12 months after completion, discusses aromatase inhibitor exposure in the endocrine-resistance context, and reports improved PFS, overall response, and clinical response in the PIK3CA-mutated cohort. Limitation: secondary review rather than original trial report.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the review text, with terminology using clinical response/benefit language.

claim_text: SOLAR-1 enrolled very few patients previously treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors; one commentary gives the PIK3CA-mutant prior-CDK4/6 figure as 5.9 percent and frames BYLieve as the prospective attempt to address the now-common sequence of progression after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy `pmid-32817061`.
evidence_summary: The commentary states that only a small number of PIK3CA-mutant HR-positive/HER2-negative SOLAR-1 patients had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, giving 5.9% or 20 patients, and describes BYLieve as a phase 2 non-comparative trial after progression on or after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy. Limitation: commentary-level source.

claim_text: Cohort C, a later-line population in which about two thirds had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, had median PFS of 5.6 months `pmid-35348782`.
evidence_summary: The BYLieve update describes Cohort C after prior chemotherapy or endocrine therapy, notes that two-thirds of patients, specifically 67.5%, had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment, and reports median PFS of 5.6 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant. Limitation: update article and non-comparative cohort.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited BYLieve update.

claim_text: In the German PRAEGNANT registry, 57 patients received alpelisib plus fulvestrant and 55 had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, directly reflecting post-CDK4/6 use outside the pivotal trial population `pmid-41925922`.
evidence_summary: The prospective German PRAEGNANT registry analysis identified 57 advanced breast cancer patients receiving alpelisib plus fulvestrant, of whom 55 had prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, explicitly motivated by limited evidence in the modern CDK4/6 inhibitor context. Limitation: small observational real-world cohort.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited registry paper.

claim_text: In an MSK retrospective cohort of 115 PIK3CA-mutant HR-positive metastatic breast cancer patients who received both everolimus and alpelisib in sequence, 71 percent had prior CDK4/6 exposure; prior CDK4/6 inhibitor use and greater treatment-line burden were associated with worse time to treatment failure, and endocrine partners differed across sequences `pmid-41620612`.
evidence_summary: The MSK single-center retrospective sequencing study included 115 PIK3CA-mutant HR-positive metastatic breast cancer patients treated sequentially with everolimus and alpelisib, reported 71% prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, found prior CDK4/6 use and more prior treatment lines associated with worse TTF in uni- and multivariable analyses, and described differing endocrine partners across sequences. Limitation: retrospective heterogeneous sequencing study.

claim_text: A post-CDK4/6 systematic review and network meta-analysis therefore appropriately cautions that cross-trial comparisons are limited by design and eligibility differences, including whether prior CDK4/6 inhibitor or chemotherapy exposure was required or permitted; it also notes that SOLAR-1 has too little prior-CDK4/6 exposure for reliable conclusions in that setting, while BYLieve was excluded from the network meta-analysis because it was non-comparative `pmid-41079023`.
evidence_summary: The systematic review and network meta-analysis states that cross-trial comparisons are limited by study design and eligibility differences including prior CDK4/6 inhibitor or chemotherapy exposure, notes SOLAR-1 had only 20 prior-CDK4/6 patients in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, and says BYLieve was excluded from the NMA because it was non-comparative. Limitation: network-level indirect comparison rather than head-to-head sequencing trial.

claim_text: A longitudinal phase I/II study of alpelisib plus an aromatase inhibitor found a 52 percent clinical benefit rate among 44 evaluable patients but identified PTEN loss-of-function mutations in 25 percent of resistant cases and expansion of ESR1 activating mutations during treatment, associated with resistance `pmid-32864625`.
evidence_summary: The longitudinal alpelisib plus aromatase inhibitor phase I/II study reports a 52% clinical benefit rate among 44 evaluable patients, loss-of-function PTEN mutations in 25% of resistant patients, and ESR1 activating mutation expansion in number and allele fraction during treatment associated with resistance. Limitation: alpelisib plus AI cohort, not fulvestrant-based SOLAR-1.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited clinical and ctDNA study.

claim_text: BYLieve subgroup reporting found no clear ESR1 interaction in Cohorts A or C, although Cohort B showed a numerical trend toward shorter PFS with ESR1 mutation, supporting the need to track endocrine partner and ESR1 status rather than treating all progression on alpelisib-endocrine therapy as PI3K escape `pmid-35348782`.
evidence_summary: The BYLieve update says ESR1 mutation analyses found no interaction in Cohorts A or C and a numerical trend toward shorter PFS with ESR1 mutations in Cohort B, where endocrine partners differed by cohort. Limitation: exploratory subgroup update with limited mechanistic resolution.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited BYLieve update.

claim_text: Earlier alpelisib plus letrozole phase Ib data also belong in this lineage: the regimen was tolerable at 300 mg daily and active in endocrine-refractory ER-positive metastatic breast cancer, especially PIK3CA-mutant disease, but it predates routine first-line CDK4/6 sequencing `pmid-27126994`.
evidence_summary: The phase Ib alpelisib plus letrozole study enrolled 26 endocrine-refractory ER-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patients, established 300 mg daily as the MTD with letrozole, and reported clinical benefit enriched in PIK3CA-mutant tumors. Limitation: small early-phase pre-routine CDK4/6 sequencing context; the paper does not address modern post-CDK4/6 treatment directly.
reviewer_notes: Supported, with the CDK4/6-era framing inferred from the 2016 early-phase context.

claim_text: The trial tested inavolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutated, endocrine-resistant advanced breast cancer after relapse during or within 12 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy; the overall-survival report describes both PFS and OS benefit, but the regimen, line of therapy, and CDK4/6 exposure context differ from alpelisib plus fulvestrant after metastatic progression `pmid-40454641`.
evidence_summary: The INAVO120 overall-survival report tested inavolisib plus palbociclib-fulvestrant versus placebo plus palbociclib-fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer recurring during or within 12 months after adjuvant endocrine therapy, and reports both PFS and OS benefit. Limitation: different PI3Kalpha inhibitor, triplet regimen, first-line/early-relapse setting, and CDK4/6 exposure context from alpelisib after metastatic progression.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited trial report.

claim_text: Biomarker reviews in this packet support the conservative bottom line: PIK3CA mutation is the established predictive biomarker for alpelisib, whereas ESR1, PTEN, AKT1, FGFR, KRAS, TP53, and longitudinal ctDNA signals remain exploratory or context-dependent for PI3K inhibitor resistance `pmid-31859350`.
evidence_summary: The biomarker review states that most response and resistance biomarkers beyond PIK3CA are retrospective or exploratory, and specifically discusses PTEN loss, Akt signaling, FGFR1/2 amplification, KRAS, TP53, ESR1/PIK3CA/AKT1 longitudinal ctDNA, while concluding PIK3CA mutation has proved predictive value for alpelisib. Limitation: review-level synthesis rather than a prospective resistance-biomarker validation study.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the cited biomarker review.
